rp-browse-04.back: Maple, Ash, Dogwood, Caprifoliaceae, Horse chestnut: opposite leaved woody plants.

rp-browse-05.back: Alternate oval leaves saw toothed mostly on the top half; purple berries with a white bloom.

rp-browse-06.back: Wedge shaped leaves 1 to 2 cm with 3 teeth at the tip, grey woolly beneath; dry slopes.

rp-browse-07.back: Opposite leaves with veins curving to the tip, white berries, bright red young stems; wet ground.

rp-browse-08.back: Evergreen, glossy sticky leaves 5 to 10 cm with 3 strong veins; dry slopes and burns.

rp-browse-09.back: Evergreen, small opposite leathery glossy toothed leaves 1 to 3 cm.

rp-browse-10.back: Willows first; red osier dogwood, cottonwood, paper birch, aspen, high bush cranberry, falsebox, subalpine fir.

rp-browse-11.back: To about 2.5 m, and they break stems down to reach higher tips.

rp-browse-12.front: How much does a moose eat a day in winter?

rp-browse-13.back: Deer tear: ragged end. Hares cut clean at about 45 degrees.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Who bit the twig? <g data-tip="Hare: clean cut|Hares and rabbits cut twigs clean at 45 degrees, like pruning shears, on stems under about 1.2 cm (75%).">

<text x="200" y="232" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">How fresh? (Tip)</text>
<g data-tip="Fresh browse|The torn end is pale green or white and moist (Tip). Browsed saskatoon in October means deer are feeding here now (Tip).">

</g>

</g>
</svg>
